note: PER-ROW OVERRIDES for the tracker rebuild (Prompt E items 5 and 7, 2026-08-20). Everything not named here is assigned by the rules in scripts/tracker-rebuild.mjs — the ballot-universe key a hunt row carries in its own Detail, then the legacy Area. This file holds the rows where a rule would land them somewhere wrong, and it holds them BY NAME so a disagreement is about one line rather than about a heuristic. RULING 32: there is no holding section, so every row here names a real section from docs/tracker-sections.json.
sectionsNote: VISUAL FEEDBACK is the section a rule cannot compute, because what makes a row one of Sean's is where it came from rather than what it touches. These are the rows opened by a pass in which he walked the product — the tester's mobile pass (2026-08-14), the copy-and-UI batch in his own words (M38-M45), and the F01 testing pass and its two continuations — plus rows whose own Detail records his ruling or his words. Everything else in this block is a row whose legacy Area sent it somewhere that is true of the work and false about who is waiting on it: a legal question is Area Data and is genuinely Sean's, and a row whose status is Blocked on the author is Sean's by definition.
prioritiesNote: RULING 29 — three levels, ranked independently inside each section and never across them. P1 is broken or blocking: something a reader hits is wrong, or work cannot proceed until this resolves. P2 is needed for the section to be done. P3 is wanted, not needed. The rebuild computes a default from the row's own status and from whether another OPEN row depends on it; this block is where that default is wrong. RULING 30 caps P1 at five per section and a section over the cap is REPORTED as stopped, never trimmed — so nothing here is a demotion to fit a number.
titlesNote: RULING 33 — a gap is a MEASUREMENT and not a task, and a count in a TITLE is a measurement wearing a task's clothes: it goes stale the next time a hunt runs, and a row whose identity is a number reads as a gap rather than as a decision. These titles name the decision. The counts are unchanged and stay in the row, where a stale one is a fact about a date rather than a lie in a heading.
